Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 53, verse 1–4:

Naming of the Surah

• It is called al-Najm (The Star), because it opens with God's oath by the star. The word "star" (al-najm) is mentioned in several other places in the Noble Qur'an, but not in the context of an oath.

Some Objectives of the Surah

• Affirming the prophethood of the Prophet (ﷺ), that he is truthful in what he conveyed, free from what the polytheists claimed about him, that the Qur'an is revelation from God, sent down through Jibril (Gabriel), and an allusion to part of the incident of the Mi'raj (Ascension) and what the Prophet (ﷺ) saw during that event.

• Refuting the claim of the polytheists that their idols are divine, and their assertion that the angels are daughters of God, and their myths about the intercession of the idols.

• Affirming that knowledge of the unseen belongs to God alone, and refuting the polytheists' analogy of the unseen world to the visible world; an allusion to the fact that the affairs of creation end with their Lord, who controls all their affairs; affirming the Resurrection, recompense, and the justice of the reckoning; a warning that directs their attention to what befell the nations that denied their messengers, and to the nearness of the Day of Resurrection, and a glimpse of its terror.

[Tafsir]

God Almighty swears by the stars when they set that Muhammad (ﷺ) has not strayed from the path of guidance and truth, nor departed from rectitude; rather, he is in the utmost uprightness, moderation and soundness, and that his speech does not proceed from his own desire. The Qur'an and the Sunnah are nothing but revelation from God to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ).

He taught Muhammad (ﷺ) a mighty angel of great strength and fine appearance, who is Jibril (peace be upon him). He appeared and rose in his true form before the Messenger (ﷺ) on the highest horizon, which is the horizon of the sun at its rising. Then Jibril drew near to the Messenger (ﷺ) and came closer still, so that his nearness was the measure of two bow-lengths or closer than that. Then Allah, glorified and exalted, revealed to His servant Muhammad (ﷺ) what He revealed, through the mediation of Jibril (peace be upon him). The heart of Muhammad (ﷺ) did not deny what his eyes saw.

Do you dispute with him over what he sees and witnesses of the signs of his Lord? And Muhammad (ﷺ) indeed saw Jibril in his true form, the form in which Allah created him, another time, at the Sidrat al-Muntaha (the Lote-Tree of the Utmost Boundary), which is a lote tree, and it is in the seventh heaven. To it ascends whatever ascends from the earth, and to it descends whatever descends from above it. Near it is the Garden of Refuge (Jannat al-Ma'wa), which was promised to the God-conscious (al-Muttaqun). When there covered the Lote-Tree that which covered it of the command of Allah, something great, whose description none knows except Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. The Prophet (ﷺ) was in a great state of steadfastness and obedience: his gaze did not swerve right or left, nor did it go beyond what he was commanded to see. Muhammad (ﷺ) indeed saw, on the night of the Ascension (al-Mi'raj), among the greatest signs of his Lord, which demonstrate Allah's power and majesty, the Garden, the Fire, and other things.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 53, verse 19–20:

Tell me, O polytheists, about these deities you worship: al-Lat, al-'Uzza, and Manat, the third, the other (goddess). Have they benefited or harmed anyone, that they should be partners with Allah?

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 53, verse 19–20:

Tell me, O polytheists, about these deities you worship: al-Lat, al-'Uzza, and Manat, the third, the other (goddess). Have they benefited or harmed anyone, that they should be partners with Allah?

Do you have for yourselves the male and for Him the female? That, then, would be an unjust division. These idols are only names, having no share of the attributes of perfection; they are names you and your fathers have given, according to your false desires. Allah has not sent down any proof for them that would confirm your claim concerning them. These polytheists follow nothing but conjecture and the desires of their own selves, which have deviated from the sound natural disposition. Yet there has come to them from their Lord, through the tongue of the Prophet (ﷺ), that which contains their guidance, but they did not benefit from it.

The Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 53, verses 27–28:

Indeed, those who do not believe in the Hereafter, from among the disbelievers of the Arabs, and do not work for it, name the angels with female names, believing in their ignorance that the angels are females and that they are daughters of Allah. They have no sound knowledge that supports what they say; they follow only conjecture, which benefits nothing and never takes the place of the truth.

So turn away from those who turn away from Our Reminder, which is the Qur'an, and who desire nothing but the life of this world. That is the extent of their knowledge and their ultimate aim. Indeed your Lord is most knowing of those who stray from the path of guidance, and He is most knowing of those who are guided and follow the path of Islam. In this is a severe warning to the sinners who turn away from acting upon the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger (ﷺ), preferring the desires of the soul and the pleasures of this world over the Hereafter.

To Allah, glorified and exalted, belongs the dominion of whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth; so that He may recompense those who did evil with their punishment for what they did of evil, and recompense those who did good with the Garden. They are those who keep away from the major sins (kaba'ir al-dhunub) and the grave immoralities (al-fawahish), except for minor lapses (al-lamam). Al-lamam are the minor sins which their doer does not persist in, or which the servant commits only rarely. Indeed, these, together with performing the obligations and abstaining from what is forbidden, Allah will forgive them and cover them over. Indeed your Lord is vast in forgiveness. He knows best your condition when He brought you forth from the earth, when He created your father Adam from dust, and when you were fetuses in the wombs of your mothers. So do not claim purity for yourselves, praising them and describing them as righteous; He knows best who has feared His punishment among His servants and so avoided His disobedience.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 53, verse 35:

Does he who turned away and gave little have knowledge of the unseen, so that he sees it (that his wealth will run out)? Has he come to know that what is in his hand will be exhausted, so that he withheld his kindness? Does he see that clearly? The matter is not so. Rather, he withheld from charity, kindness, goodness and kinship, out of stinginess and miserliness.
Or has he not been told of what is in the books of the Torah and the scrolls of Ibrahim, who fulfilled what he was commanded and conveyed it?
Or has he not been told of what is in the books of the Torah and the scrolls of Ibrahim, who fulfilled what he was commanded and conveyed it?
That no soul will be held to account for the sin of another, and no one will bear its burden for it, and that a person will receive no reward except for what he himself has striven for.

And that his effort will be seen in the Hereafter, so that his good deeds are distinguished from his evil ones: an honor for the doer of good and a rebuke for the wrongdoer.
Then man will be recompensed for his striving with the full reward for all of his deeds, and that to your Lord, O Messenger, is the final return of all His creation on the Day of Resurrection.

And that He, glorified and exalted, makes whom He wills laugh in this world by granting him joy, and makes whom He wills weep by afflicting him with grief.

And that He, glory be to Him, causes death to whomever He wills of His creation, and gives life to whomever He wills of them. So He alone, glory be to Him, is the One who has sole control over giving life and causing death.
And that He created the pairs, the male and the female, among humankind and animals, from a drop of semen that is poured into the womb.

And that, to your Lord, O Messenger, belongs the bringing back of their creation after their death, which is the second creation (al-nashʾah al-ukhrā) on the Day of Resurrection.
And that it is He who enriches whom He wills of His creation with wealth, and gives them possession of it and makes them content with it.

And that He, glorified and exalted, is the Lord of al-Shi'ra (Sirius). It is a bright star, which some of the people of the jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance before Islam) used to worship besides Allah.

And that He, glory be to Him, destroyed the first ʿĀd, who were the people of Hūd, and destroyed Thamūd, who were the people of Ṣāliḥ, and He left none of them remaining. And before them He destroyed the people of Nūḥ. These were more defiant in rebellion and greater in disbelief than those who came after them. And the cities of the people of Lūṭ — God overturned them upon them, and made their uppermost part their lowermost, and covered them with what covered them of stones following one another, descending upon them from the sky like rain.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 53, verse 55:

﴿Then which of the favors of your Lord, O disbelieving human, will you doubt?﴾
This is Muhammad ﷺ, a warner with the truth, the same truth with which the prophets before him warned. So he is not a novelty among the messengers.
The Hour has drawn near, and its time has approached. None other than Allah can then avert it, and none knows the time of its occurrence except Allah.
